Title: Diagnosis
Details: The corresponding issue report describes that tooltip text in the UI is displayed with HTML entities such as " instead of the intended characters. This strongly suggests a missing escaping or decoding step in tooltip generation. Inspecting the implementation of StandardToolTipTagFragmentGenerator.generateToolTipFragment reveals that it directly returns the toolTipText without applying any escaping. Recent issue reports mention similar encoding or escaping problems in related UI components, reinforcing the suspicion that this method lacks proper handling. The behavior observed in the code matches the issue report's symptoms, indicating that missing escaping in this method is the likely root cause.

After providing this diagnosis, you will be prompted to suggest which methods would be the best locations to be fixed. The answers should be in the form of `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` without commentary (one per line), as your answer will be automatically processed before finally being presented to the user.

Title: Diagnosis
Details: The failing test `isUnixSymlinkIsFalseIfMoreThanOneFlagIsSet` checks that when a Zip entry has more than one Unix permission flag set, `isUnixSymlink` returns false. The current bug report describes a problem where `isUnixSymlink` returns true for Zip entries with Unix permissions `177777` (i.e., multiple flags set, including the symlink bit and others). 

Examining the code of `ZipArchiveEntry.isUnixSymlink()` reveals that it returns true if `(getUnixMode() & UnixStat.LINK_FLAG) == UnixStat.LINK_FLAG`. The `UnixStat.LINK_FLAG` is a constant `0120000` (octal), representing the Unix file mode for a symlink. The method `getUnixMode()` extracts Unix permission bits by shifting and masking the external attributes, but it returns the full permission mode. 

The issue is that `isUnixSymlink()` tests only if the LINK_FLAG bit is set, and does not require that *only* the `LINK_FLAG` bit is set. So if multiple permission bits are set including the symlink flag (such as `177777`), `isUnixSymlink` will incorrectly return true. The failing test attempts to catch this logic flaw by using a Zip entry with multiple flags, expecting `isUnixSymlink()` to return false.

Recent ticket and the current bug report indicate this problem originates from Commons Compress, not from the source of the Zip file.

In summary, the bug happened because `isUnixSymlink()` only tests if the symlink bit is set in the Unix mode, not that the symlink bit is the only bit set. This leads to false positives where multiple bits including symlink being set returns true, which is incorrect.

To fix this, `isUnixSymlink()` should be changed to ensure that the mode bits indicate a symlink exclusively (i.e., mode == LINK_FLAG), not just that the symlink bit is among other bits set.

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
